mechanism_narrative: The recent upward trend in RETAIL_REC mobility, evidenced by its highest value in the last four weeks at t-0w, indicates a sustained recovery in consumer activity that will continue to drive retail and recreation footfall higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days, despite the recent upward momentum.

mechanism_narrative: A significant week-on-week rebound in PARKS mobility, as observed from t-1w to t-0w, signals increased willingness for out-of-home activities and leisure, which will spill over into higher RETAIL_REC within the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by more than 10 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within the next two weeks following a week-on-week PARKS increase greater than 10 points.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent week-on-week increases in both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility suggest a return to office-based work and commuting, which typically boosts weekday retail and recreation activity, leading to higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both show week-on-week increases
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines over the next four weeks despite concurrent week-on-week increases in both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility, observed from t-1w to t-0w, indicates that people are spending less time at home, which directly translates to more opportunities and inclination for out-of-home activities, including retail and recreation, over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve over the next four weeks, even if RESIDENTIAL mobility continues to decline.

mechanism_narrative: After two consecutive weeks of decline, the week-on-week increase in GROCERY_PHARM mobility at t-0w signifies a stabilization of essential shopping patterns, potentially freeing up consumer time and discretionary spending for non-essential retail and recreation within the next week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM increases week-on-week after two consecutive weeks of decline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decreases in the next week despite GROCERY_PHARM showing a week-on-week increase after a prior decline.

mechanism_narrative: The inverse relationship between RESIDENTIAL and RETAIL_REC mobility implies that as people spend less time at home, they engage more in retail and recreation. The recent decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility suggests a continued shift towards out-of-home activities, boosting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines over the next four weeks while RESIDENTIAL mobility also declines.

mechanism_narrative: The strong rebound in PARKS mobility in mid-August (t-0w) indicates a peak in summer outdoor activities. Historically, this seasonal peak often precedes a shift towards indoor retail and recreation as weather changes, leading to a positive spillover for RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS mobility is above 25% change from baseline in mid-August
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve over the next four weeks, or PARKS mobility drops sharply immediately after the observed peak.

mechanism_narrative: A divergence where WORKPLACES mobility stabilizes or slightly increases while RESIDENTIAL mobility decreases indicates a clear shift away from home-centric activities towards out-of-home work and leisure, which will directly boost retail and recreation over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES shows a week-on-week increase or stabilization (change >= 0) while RESIDENTIAL shows a week-on-week decrease
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines within the next two weeks even when WORKPLACES stabilizes/increases and RESIDENTIAL decreases.
